description: Operational health of the Altinn information portal (info.altinn.no, Umbraco) in production. Availability comes from the blackbox-exporter probes in admin-prod-obs-amw; traffic, latency, exceptions and dependencies come from Application Insights (dis-core-prod-products-ai, cloud_RoleName=infoportal). Datasource UIDs are pinned rather than templated so the panels cannot silently bind to the wrong Prometheus.

panels.title: /health right now
panels.description: Deep health check: HTTP 200 **and** a JSON body of `status: Healthy`. This is the exact series the `Availability Prod` alert evaluates.

panels.title: /health availability
panels.description: Fraction of the selected range where the deep /health probe passed. Prober pods are collapsed with `max by (instance)` **before** averaging over time, so a short-lived replica cannot mask an outage.

panels.title: /health downtime
panels.description: Minutes of failing /health inside the selected range.

panels.title: Front page availability
panels.description: Shallow HTTP probe (ipv4 + ipv6) of `https://info.altinn.no` — reachable, TLS valid, HTTP 200. Compare against /health: the site can serve pages perfectly while the application reports itself unhealthy.

panels.title: TLS cert expires in
panels.description: Days until the earliest certificate in the chain expires.

panels.title: /health probe duration
panels.description: Wall-clock time of the most recent deep health probe.

panels.title: Probe status over time — deep /health vs shallow HTTP
panels.description: Each band is Up/Down over time. The deep /health probe and the shallow HTTP probes disagree during application-level incidents: the front page keeps serving while /health reports unhealthy. Outages show as contiguous red blocks rather than flapping.

panels.title: Probe duration by job
panels.description: The deep check runs the full application health pipeline, so it is expected to be slower than the shallow probes.

panels.title: Traffic summary (selected range)

azureLogAnalytics.query:
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal"
| summarize
    Requests = count(),
    Success = countif(toint(resultCode) between (200 .. 399)),
    NotFound = countif(resultCode == "404"),
    ServerErrors = countif(toint(resultCode) >= 500)
| extend ErrorRatePct = round(100.0 * ServerErrors / Requests, 3)

panels.description: `NotFound` is deliberately **not** counted as an error — 404s dominate this service (see the Not-found row) and would otherwise drown the real signal. `ErrorRatePct` is 5xx only.

panels.title: Requests by status class

azureLogAnalytics.query:
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal"
| extend Class = case(
    toint(resultCode) >= 500, "5xx",
    toint(resultCode) >= 400, "4xx",
    toint(resultCode) >= 300, "3xx",
    toint(resultCode) >= 200, "2xx",
    "other")
| summarize Count = count() by bin(timestamp, $__interval), Class
| order by timestamp asc

panels.description: Stacked request volume. The 4xx band is almost entirely 404 noise from clients aiming Altinn API paths at this host.

panels.title: Server latency percentiles (404s excluded)

azureLogAnalytics.query:
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal"
| where resultCode != "404"
| summarize
    p50 = percentile(duration, 50),
    p95 = percentile(duration, 95),
    p99 = percentile(duration, 99)
  by bin(timestamp, $__interval)
| order by timestamp asc

panels.description: 404s are excluded because they short-circuit in ~30 ms and would flatten the percentiles for real traffic. Recurring p99 spikes into the seconds come from `POST /api/contactform/send`.

panels.title: Endpoints — volume, outcome and latency

azureLogAnalytics.query:
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal"
| extend Endpoint = replace_regex(
    replace_regex(name, @"/\d{6,}", "/{orgnr}"),
    @"/[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}",
    "/{guid}")
| summarize
    Count = count(),
    Ok = countif(toint(resultCode) between (200 .. 399)),
    NotFound = countif(resultCode == "404"),
    Err5xx = countif(toint(resultCode) >= 500),
    P95ms = round(percentile(duration, 95), 1),
    P99ms = round(percentile(duration, 99), 1)
  by Endpoint
| extend OkPct = round(100.0 * Ok / Count, 1)
| project Endpoint, Count, OkPct, NotFound, Err5xx, P95ms, P99ms
| order by Count desc
| take 30

panels.description: Org numbers and GUIDs are normalised to `{orgnr}` / `{guid}`; without that the un-routed 404 paths explode into thousands of one-off rows. Sort by P99ms to find slow endpoints.

panels.title: Not found (404) — the dominant traffic class, tracked apart from errors
404s — CMS content vs unknown API path

azureLogAnalytics.query:
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal"
| where resultCode == "404"
| extend Kind = iff(name has "umbraco", "CMS content", "Unknown API path")
| summarize Count = count() by bin(timestamp, $__interval), Kind
| order by timestamp asc

panels.description: Two very different problems. **CMS content** = a real content lookup that missed, i.e. broken links or unpublished nodes — actionable by the content team. **Unknown API path** = clients calling Altinn API routes that this portal never served — actionable by whoever owns those clients or the routing.

panels.title: Who is still calling removed endpoints

azureLogAnalytics.query:
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal" and resultCode == "404"
| extend UA = tostring(customDimensions["user_agent.original"])
| extend Caller = iff(isempty(UA), "(no user-agent)", UA)
| extend Endpoint = replace_regex(name, @"/\d{6,}", "/{orgnr}")
| summarize N = count(), Last = max(timestamp) by Caller, Endpoint
| summarize
    Requests = sum(N),
    Endpoints = dcount(Endpoint),
    LastSeen = max(Last),
    (TopN, TopEndpoint) = arg_max(N, Endpoint)
  by Caller
| project Caller, Requests, Endpoints, TopEndpoint, LastSeen
| order by Requests desc
| take 25

panels.description:
Attribution for the 404 flood, by client `user_agent.original`.

**Read `Endpoints` to tell the two populations apart.** A legacy integration hammers **one** endpoint at high volume (`python-requests` → `/api/{orgnr}/messages`, `SAP NetWeaver` → `/api/authentication/…`); a scanner sprays **hundreds** of distinct paths at low volume (`leaky/0.1`, `curl`).

**Note on referers:** no `Referer` is captured — these are server-to-server API clients, which don't send one. The user agent is the attribution signal. Source IP is *not* usable either: every request arrives via Cloudflare, so `http.client_ip` is a CDN edge node rather than the origin.

panels.title: Top 404 paths, by caller

azureLogAnalytics.query:
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal" and resultCode == "404"
| extend UA = tostring(customDimensions["user_agent.original"])
| extend Caller = iff(isempty(UA), "(no user-agent)", UA)
| extend Path = replace_regex(
    replace_regex(name, @"/\d{6,}", "/{orgnr}"),
    @"/[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}",
    "/{guid}")
| summarize Requests = count(), LastSeen = max(timestamp) by Path, Caller
| order by Requests desc
| take 30

panels.description: The same 404s broken out per (path, caller) pair — this is the table to hand to whoever owns a legacy client, since it names both the dead endpoint and who is still calling it. Filter the Caller column to isolate one integration.

panels.title: Exceptions — the same grouping the 'Exceptions Prod' alert uses
Trace volume by severity

azureLogAnalytics.query:
traces
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal"
| extend Severity = case(
    severityLevel >= 4, "Critical",
    severityLevel == 3, "Error",
    severityLevel == 2, "Warning",
    "Info")
| summarize Count = count() by bin(timestamp, $__interval), Severity
| order by timestamp asc

panels.description: `severityLevel >= 3` (Error/Critical) is what pages Slack. This service uses the `traces` table for exceptions; the App Insights `exceptions` table is empty.

panels.title: Top exceptions (Type / Details / Count)

azureLogAnalytics.query:
traces
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal"
| where severityLevel >= 3
| extend ExType = tostring(customDimensions.["exception.type"])
| extend ExMsg = tostring(customDimensions.["exception.message"])
| extend Details = iff(isnotempty(ExMsg), ExMsg, message)
| summarize Count = count(), LastSeen = max(timestamp)
  by Type = ExType, Details = substring(Details, 0, 200)
| project Type, Details, Count, LastSeen
| order by Count desc
| take 25

panels.description: Grouped identically to `rules-exceptions.yaml`, so a Slack alert line maps 1:1 onto a row here — widen the time range to see how long it has been recurring.

panels.title: Dependencies by target

azureLogAnalytics.query:
dependencies
| where cloud_RoleName == "infoportal"
| summarize
    Count = count(),
    Failures = countif(success == false),
    P95ms = round(percentile(duration, 95), 1)
  by Type = type, Target = target
| extend FailPct = round(100.0 * Failures / Count, 1)
| project Type, Target, Count, Failures, FailPct, P95ms
| order by Count desc
| take 25

panels.description: Low call counts are normal here — most of the site is served from the Umbraco cache. A target at 100% FailPct with only a handful of calls is still a real outage of that integration (e.g. site search), not a rounding artefact.

title: Infoportal — Service Health (Prod)
